title: Recovered work
originalRequest: Establish an automated pipeline to ingest, digitize, validate, and analyze handwritten weather logs from the Cape Point lighthouse keeper's journal (1880-1920).
latestMessage: Establish an automated pipeline to ingest, digitize, validate, and analyze handwritten weather logs from the Cape Point lighthouse keeper's journal (1880-1920).

steps.title: Database Schema Definition
steps.instruction: Define the SQL database schema to store transcribed weather variables including barometric pressure, wind speed, wind direction, visibility, and precipitation.
steps.acceptance: Schema includes tables for journals, daily entries, sub-daily observations, and keeper metadata. Foreign key constraints are established.
steps.result: Database schema designed and implemented in PostgreSQL. Schema validation scripts passed and initial migrations were applied.

steps.title: OCR Model Training and Calibration
steps.instruction: Fine-tune a handwritten text recognition (HTR) model on a curated dataset of the historical lighthouse keeper's handwriting samples.
steps.acceptance: Character Error Rate (CER) is below 5% on the validation set.
steps.result: Model training completed over 50 epochs. Final CER is 4.2% on the validation set, meeting the acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Ingestion Pipeline for Scanned Logbooks
steps.instruction: Develop an ingestion script to process high-resolution TIFF images of the journal pages, split them into page pairs, and register them with unique identifiers.
steps.acceptance: All 1,460 scanned pages are successfully cataloged in the database with correct page numbering.
steps.result: Ingestion pipeline written in Python. Successfully processed and cataloged 1,460 pages from the 1880-1920 archive.

steps.title: Transcription Validation System
steps.instruction: Implement a verification module to cross-check transcribed values against physical limits and highlight anomalies.
steps.acceptance: Flagging logic triggers on invalid ranges and flags entries for manual verification.
steps.result: Attempt 3 in progress. Attempt 1 failed due to false positives in high-wind velocity scales. Attempt 2 resolved scale issues but failed to handle missing data fields. Currently rewriting the validation parser to handle null fields and pressure drops during historical storms.

steps.title: Wind Direction Vectorization
steps.instruction: Parse compass points from transcribed logs and convert them to degrees (0-360) for numerical analysis.
steps.acceptance: All standard 16-point compass directions mapped correctly, unknown entries flagged as null.
steps.result: Mapping dictionary implemented and applied to the database. All directional strings parsed and numerical degree values populated.

steps.title: Barometric Pressure Standardization
steps.instruction: Convert raw pressure entries recorded in inches of mercury to hectopascals and apply temperature correction adjustments where noted.
steps.acceptance: All converted values are stored in a standardized hPa column with precision to two decimal places.
steps.result: Implemented conversion algorithm using standard physical formulas. Applied temperature offsets based on marginalia notes.

steps.title: Keeper Metadata Association
steps.instruction: Extract and correlate the active lighthouse keeper's identity with each daily log entry based on shift schedules and hand-written signatures.
steps.acceptance: All log entries are successfully mapped to a specific keeper ID in the database.
steps.result: Extracted signature patterns and matched them with historical employment records. All entries mapped to keepers.

steps.title: Precipitation Accumulation Normalization
steps.instruction: Normalize precipitation entries recorded in buckets or inches into standard millimeters, accounting for historical gauge dimensions.
steps.acceptance: Data conversion function created and tested; database column for precip_mm populated.
steps.result: Conversion logic applied successfully. Verified that historical gauge adjustments were correctly scaled to modern millimeter standards.

steps.title: Data Export API Development
steps.instruction: Create a REST API endpoint to export the normalized weather dataset in JSON and CSV formats for external climate researchers.
steps.acceptance: Endpoints support querying by date range, keeper, and specific weather variables with pagination.
steps.result: API developed using FastAPI. Endpoints tested and confirmed returning accurate datasets matching query parameters.

steps.title: Missing Data Interpolation
steps.instruction: Implement a linear interpolation method for short gaps in barometric pressure data to ensure continuous timeseries analysis.
steps.acceptance: Interpolated values are flagged with a specific quality flag and do not override raw entries.
steps.result: Interpolation script runs as a post-processing step. Quality flag metadata updated correctly across all gap-filled entries.

steps.title: Final Quality Assurance Audit
steps.instruction: Perform a final end-to-end audit on a randomized sample of 5% of the total dataset to verify transcription and conversion accuracy.
steps.acceptance: Error rate in the sampled dataset is below 1% for all weather variables.
steps.result: Audit completed by verifier agent. Selected 73 random pages representing 1,500 observation points. Manual cross-verification showed a transcription discrepancy rate of 0.35% and conversion error rate of 0.00%. The dataset is verified as clean and accurate.
